body: You came in serious. From early on, being yourself felt like something to prove, so you built an identity out of effort and discipline. You don't expect things handed to you. You expect to earn them. This can feel like approval is conditional, especially around authority, standards, or self-respect. You may overwork to feel worthy, or hold yourself back before anyone can judge you. Here's the part nobody mentions: you age into your power. You get more solid, more real, more yourself every decade. The work is building self-respect from the inside instead of waiting to be handed it.
gift: At your best: self-made, credible, an authority that's actually earned.
shadow: The trap: harsh self-judgment, and waiting for a permission that never arrives.
integration: Let identity and discipline and limits cooperate without making either one carry the whole story. Disciplined and reliable; the risk is self-limiting caution and joyless striving.
do: Define enough on your own terms
Build self-respect instead of waiting for it
Let yourself be a late bloomer
